NAAVIK GAMING PODCAST
The Black Friday Playbook: How Game Publishers Can Maximize Holiday Sales
By Kalie Moore   •   November 10, 2026
Black Friday is the biggest week of the year for game sales, and the decisions that shape it happen long before players hit buy.
Julian Migura
, co-founder and COO of
VaultN
, joins
Kalie Moore
to walk through how publishers should plan the holiday window, using data from VaultN’s network of publishers and storefronts. They cover how deep to discount, on what channels and best practices for how to protect your price for the rest of the year. They also discuss what Valve ending physical Steam gift cards means for gifting, why marketplaces like Amazon still can’t sell PC game codes, and where players will be buying games next.

Kalie:
Welcome to the Naavik Gaming Podcast. I'm your host, Kalie Moore. When you listen to this, we will be officially 2.5 weeks out from Black Friday, which is the biggest week of the year for game sales.
And while you, or maybe the gamers in your life, might be asking what's going on sale on Steam, the publishers are asking themselves different kind of questions long before anyone hits buy. How deep do you discount? Where do you discount first? And how do you avoid burning your price for the rest of the year in a single long weekend?
My guests today see this, those decisions play out in data. Julian Migura is the co-founder and COO of VaultN, the infrastructure that connects publishers to storefronts selling their games beyond Steam. Take-Two, Microsoft Gaming, Bethesda all use it, and publishers have received more than 100 million in royalties through the platform this year.
According to VaultN's publishing partner data, close to 40% of a year's game units sell in Q4. Black Friday week alone moves about 15% of those, and the week after Christmas often beats Christmas itself because that's when people finally have the time and the gift money to spend. This year, there's a new wrinkle.
Valve has stopped restocking physical Steam gift cards, so the easiest way for a grandparent to gift a game has disappeared from sho- from store shelves. Today, we're gonna talk about how publishers should plan for that holiday window, where third-party sales fit alongside Steam, and the new places players are starting to buy.
Julian, welcome to the podcast.
Julian:
Hi, Kalie. Thank you for having me.
Kalie:
All right. I wanna talk a little bit about your background before we dive into Black Friday best practices. You spent years in Brazil and Latin America in games payments, and you helped bring Steam to the region. What did watching players try to pay for games there teach you about where sales actually get lost?
Julian:
Yeah, exactly. I started to work in the games industry about 20 years ago, and I think about 15 years or so ago started working on the, the payment side. And we noticed that this was a big issue. I actually worked in publishing before, where we had the same troubling problems of getting users to convert in Latin America.
And what we see here is basically that in markets with limited accessibility, which Brazil and Latin America is certainly one of those, most of the sales happen essentially at the checkout, not as discovery. That means that if you don't have the ability to charge a user. There is, like you have a lack of the local payment methods that you support, or you don't have pricing in local currency, then there's a very high risk that you will not convert the demand that is there.
So, the demand is there. It's always there. It's always been there, and people will get excited. There was a large number of Brazilians who learned Korean just in order to play the first MMOs when they were released in Korea. So, there was a big community there playing a game that was solely available in Korean at the time.
So, the demand was definitely there and is definitely there, and was never the problem. The players want to play the game. Yeah, but you're essentially losing them at the time that they're locking in the spend, so to say. And that is simply because they have no ability to buy.
Kalie:
Got it. So, I wanna hear a little bit more about VaultN just for background before we dive into things.
So, I know that VaultN solves PC distribution at scale. Can you walk me through what that actually means?
Julian:
Yeah, of course. So basically, we're enabling publishers to go to where the players are, so to be on every shelf, digital shelf for that matter mostly, and in every market. So, find better routes to the players, cut the costs of operating those routes, make it more efficient, make it automatic, and essentially provide an infrastructure that re- reduces the cost and the risk for publishers to operate with those channels while keeping full control and, and real-time visibility, and we can see that that adds 25 to 30% more revenue, more PC revenue globally and, you know, 40 to 50% in specific markets.
Kalie:
Okay. So now that we have the background, let's dive into the data. So, as I mentioned at the top, you told me close to 40% of a year's units sell in Q4, and most of that is from basically Black Friday onward.
So, when a publisher comes into November, what actually changes about how they make decisions compared to the rest of the year when it comes to promotions?
